source_book: NCERT Class 11 Physics Ch.7 System of Particles and Rotational Motion §7.9 (rotational kinetic energy; work done by a torque) — table-of-contents scope only, teaching authored from first principles; no example, derivation order or figure imported from any textbook (DC Pandey check: chapter table of contents only). The atomic concept: a constant torque acting through an angle does work on a rotating body, W = τθ, and that work equals the change in the body's rotational kinetic energy, KE = ½Iω² — the rotational work-energy theorem. Does NOT cover what torque is (torque), how I is computed (moment_of_inertia), how a torque produces angular acceleration (tau_eq_i_alpha), angular momentum (angular_momentum), or the kinetic-energy split in rolling motion (pure_rolling, rolling_on_incline). Built on the rigid_body_rotation field_3d engine (0c-1, docs/loop_runs/rotmech/), pure configuration, zero renderer edits.

real_world_anchor.primary: A bicycle wheel spun by hand, then slowed by squeezing its brake — the exact system rendered.
real_world_anchor.secondary: A potter's wheel slowed by a hand pressed to its rim, the hand growing warm as the wheel slows.

aha_moment.statement: The brake's work on the wheel exactly equals the kinetic energy it loses.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: The energy meter and its bar fall while the work counter grows more negative, beat for beat, the same amount each time.

I_frame.name: Fixed apparatus inertia (bare turntable, no masses)

m.name: Mass of each of the two symmetric sliding masses on the rod — apparatus-fixed in this concept, no slider anywhere

r.name: Distance of each mass from the axle — apparatus-fixed in this concept, no slider anywhere (moment-of-inertia dependence belongs to moment_of_inertia, not this concept)

I.name: Total moment of inertia of the turntable plus two masses — CONSTANT in every state of this concept (no param_ramp on r, no m/r slider anywhere)

omega0.name: Angular speed the wheel is spinning at when a state's clock begins (the seed value) — every guided state reseeds this value fresh

omega.name: Live angular speed — the engine's own derived quantity; documented here as the closed form the decay follows while the brake is engaged and the wheel has not yet stopped

tau_brake.name: Magnitude of the constant frictional brake torque opposing the spin — the guided value is 0.40 (forced by the 0.05-step slider grid, not taste)

tau.name: Net RESOLVED torque the wheel actually feels — reads exactly 0 once the wheel is at rest (rest clamp), never the authored schedule value

alpha.name: Angular acceleration — the engine's own per-step finite difference of omega; equals the closed form below everywhere except the rest-clamp/engage edges (I is constant here, so no dI/dt term ever enters)

theta.name: Angle turned since the torque began acting in THIS state's own local clock (time-integrated)

KE.name: Rotational kinetic energy — time-varying whenever the brake is engaged; equals 0.5*I*omega0^2 only at/near a state's own t=0

W.name: Signed work done on the wheel by the torque since THIS state's own run anchor (re-zeroes at every state entry — correct per-state ledger behaviour, not a bug)

formulas.moment_of_inertia: I = I_frame + 2*m*r^2 — CONSTANT throughout this concept: no state authors a param_ramp on r, and neither r nor m is ever exposed as a slider. I = 3.06 kg·m^2 in every single state, STATE_1 through STATE_6.
formulas.angular_decay_under_constant_torque: While the brake is engaged and the wheel has not yet stopped: omega(t) = omega0 - (tau_brake/I)*t and theta(t) = omega0*t - 0.5*(tau_brake/I)*t^2, t measured from the instant the brake engages in that state's own local clock. The rest clamp holds omega = theta_dot = 0 for all t >= t_stop = omega0*I/tau_brake.
formulas.net_torque_and_alpha: tau (the PRINTED row) = -tau_brake while omega>0, else exactly 0 (rest clamp) — the net torque the integrator is actually running, never the authored schedule value. alpha (the PRINTED row) is the engine's own per-step finite difference of omega; away from the t=0/engage/rest-clamp edges it equals the analytic -tau_brake/I exactly, because I is constant everywhere in this concept.
formulas.rotational_kinetic_energy: KE = 0.5*I*omega^2 = L^2/(2I) (numerically identical forms; this concept never displays L).
formulas.work_torque_times_angle: W = tau*theta, identically BY CONSTRUCTION inside the engine's own integrator (theta and W accumulate from the same grid-walk operand) — this identity never drifts at any pinned instant, for any reachable tau_brake.
formulas.work_energy_theorem: For constant I: W = delta(KE) = KE - KE0 over the SAME interval (the work-energy theorem for rotation) — holds to within one display quantum (<= 0.01 J), except at the exact full-stop frame, where a shared grid-quantization theta bias pushes the printed W one quantum past the printed delta-KE. No state is ever pinned at the full stop.

constraints: I = I_frame + 2*m*r^2 = 3.06 kg·m^2 at every instant in every state — r and m never change (no slider, no ramp, anywhere in this concept).
tau (printed) is the RESOLVED net torque, not the authored schedule value: it reads exactly 0.00 once omega = 0 (rest clamp), and -tau_brake at every instant before that.

alpha (printed) is a finite difference of omega, not tau/I evaluated: stays correct at the rest clamp and at every engage edge; equals -tau_brake/I exactly away from those edges, because I is constant here.
W is IDENTICALLY tau*theta by construction (never merely approximate) — checkable at any pinned instant, in every state that shows theta, tau and W together.
W = delta(KE) over the same interval to within one display quantum, except at the exact full-stop frame — no state is ever pinned there.
W is the SIGNED work integral and re-zeroes at every state's own run anchor (a fresh state entry is a fresh anchor) — never narrated as one continuous run across states.
tau_brake is reachable only in 0.05 N·m steps over [0, 2.0]; omega0 only in 0.1 rad/s steps over [0, 3.0] — a guided value outside these grids can never be reproduced by a teacher's slider.
m, r and the drum radius have NO on-screen instrument anywhere in this concept and must never be spoken or quoted, in any state, in any language.

assessment.mastery_definition: A student masters this concept if they can state that a spinning body has kinetic energy even when it does not travel, predict how rotational kinetic energy falls as the square of angular speed, compute the work done by a constant torque as W = τθ, explain what a negative sign on that work means, and state that the work done by a torque on a rotating body equals the change in its rotational kinetic energy.

questions.stem: A flywheel spins steadily on a fixed axle, and its centre stays in exactly the same place the whole time. Does the flywheel have kinetic energy?

options.A: Yes — every part of the spinning flywheel is moving, so it has rotational kinetic energy, KE = ½Iω²
options.B: No — kinetic energy requires the object's centre to move through space
options.C: Only once the flywheel starts slowing down
options.D: Only if an external force is acting on it right now

distractor_misconceptions.B: Confuses kinetic energy with translational motion of the centre of mass, missing that every point on a spinning body is still moving.
distractor_misconceptions.C: Assumes kinetic energy appears only when something changes, rather than whenever mass is actually in motion.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Confuses the condition for a CHANGE in kinetic energy (a net torque) with the condition for kinetic energy to exist at all (motion).

questions.parallel_form_stem: A ceiling fan spins steadily with its centre bolted in place. Does the fan have kinetic energy while it spins?

questions.stem: A brake cuts a wheel's angular speed exactly in half, from ω to ω/2. What happens to its rotational kinetic energy?

options.A: It falls to one quarter of its original value
options.B: It falls to half its original value, matching the drop in speed
options.C: It stays the same, since only the speed changed, not the mass distribution
options.D: It falls to one eighth of its original value

distractor_misconceptions.B: Assumes kinetic energy scales linearly with speed, the same mistake as assuming K = mv instead of K = ½mv² for straight-line motion.
distractor_misconceptions.C: Assumes kinetic energy depends only on how the mass is arranged (I), missing that KE = ½Iω² also depends on speed.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Confuses squaring the speed ratio (ω² → (ω/2)² = ω²/4) with cubing it.

questions.parallel_form_stem: A spinning turntable's speed is cut to exactly a third of its original value. By what factor does its rotational kinetic energy fall?

questions.stem: A constant torque of 5.0 N·m acts on a wheel while it turns through an angle of 3.0 radians. How much work does the torque do on the wheel?

options.D: The answer cannot be found without knowing how long the torque acted

distractor_misconceptions.B: Adds torque and angle instead of multiplying them.
distractor_misconceptions.C: Divides torque by angle instead of multiplying them.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Believes work needs a time duration, confusing work (force or torque acting through a distance or angle) with power (work per unit time).

questions.parallel_form_stem: A torque of 2.0 N·m acts on a rotating shaft while it turns through 4.0 radians. How much work does the torque do?

questions.stem: A brake applies a torque that opposes a spinning wheel, and the wheel is slowing down. The work done by the brake's torque is negative. What does that negative sign mean?

options.A: The brake is removing energy from the wheel
options.B: No work is actually being done, since the wheel is losing speed rather than gaining it
options.C: The brake's torque is pointed the wrong way and should be reversed
options.D: The same amount of work was done, just measured in the opposite direction

distractor_misconceptions.B: Assumes work requires a gain in speed, missing that a torque doing negative work is still doing real work — it is removing energy.
distractor_misconceptions.C: Misreads the sign of the work as an error in the torque's direction, rather than a report of energy leaving the body.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Treats the sign as a measurement convention rather than the direction of energy flow.

questions.parallel_form_stem: A hand presses on a spinning bicycle wheel's rim, and the wheel slows down. The hand's torque does negative work on the wheel. What does that tell you?

questions.stem: As a torque does negative work on a spinning wheel, what happens to the wheel's rotational kinetic energy?

options.A: It falls by exactly the amount of work done
options.B: It stays the same, as long as no external force acts on the wheel's centre
options.C: It falls, but by an amount unrelated to the work done
options.D: It only changes if the wheel is also moving through space

distractor_misconceptions.B: Confuses the condition for kinetic energy to change (work done by a torque) with a condition about forces on the centre of mass.
distractor_misconceptions.C: Misses the rotational work-energy theorem entirely — the work done IS the change in kinetic energy, not merely correlated with it.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Confuses rotational kinetic energy with translational kinetic energy, assuming energy can only change if the body travels somewhere.

questions.parallel_form_stem: A torque does 12 J of negative work on a spinning disc as it slows down. By how much does the disc's rotational kinetic energy change?

questions.stem: For a rotating body, torque τ equals Iα, and angle relates to angular speed by dθ = ω dt. Carrying W = ∫τ dθ through with these two relations gives which result?

options.A: W = Δ(½Iω²), the change in rotational kinetic energy
options.B: W = Iα², a term with no direct physical meaning here
options.C: W = Iω, the angular momentum of the body

distractor_misconceptions.B: Substitutes τ = Iα incorrectly, squaring α instead of carrying the integral through to completion.
distractor_misconceptions.C: Confuses the work integral's result with the definition of angular momentum, a different quantity entirely.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Drops the ω dt substitution partway through, leaving a term built only from α.

questions.parallel_form_stem: Starting from W = ∫τ dθ, substitute τ = Iα and dθ = ω dt, then integrate. What single expression does the work simplify to?

scene_composition.text: The wheel spins steadily — nothing external acts on it yet
I, omega and KE build in one at a time: I = 3.06, omega = 1.50, KE = 3.44 joules
the wheel's centre never moves, yet every part of it is moving

tts_sentences.text_en: Two masses set this rod's moment of inertia, I: three point zero six kilogram metre squared.
It turns at one point five zero radians per second, angular speed omega, though its centre never moves.
The kinetic energy meter reads three point four four joules — nothing travels, yet the energy is real.

misconception_watch.belief: Kinetic energy means going somewhere — this wheel stays in one place, so it has none.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The wheel's centre never moves, every part of it still traces a circle at real speed, and the meter reads 3.44 J the whole time.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Every part of a spinning body is moving, so a turning body has kinetic energy — for rotation it is one half I omega squared.

STATE_2.title: Half the speed, quarter the energy

scene_composition.text: The brake pad travels in and presses onto the wheel's rim
Speed falls from 1.50 toward 0.75 rad/s while energy falls from 3.44 toward 0.86 joules — a quarter left
like a bicycle wheel slowed by squeezing its brake

tts_sentences.text_en: Like a bicycle wheel slowed by squeezing its brake, the pad presses onto this wheel's rim.
The energy bar empties far faster than the speed drops.
Speed omega falls toward half, zero point seven five radians per second; kinetic energy falls to a quarter, zero point eight six joules.

misconception_watch.belief: Take away half the speed and you take away half the energy.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The chips are placed first — ½ of 1.50 on the speed row, ¼ of 3.44 on the energy row — then the live readouts walk down onto them, and the bar is three quarters empty when the speed has only halved.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The energy depends on the speed squared, so halving the speed leaves only a quarter of the energy.

scene_composition.text: The brake keeps acting — its turning effect is the torque tau
Angle theta and work W climb together while the torque meter holds at −0.40 N·m
the minus sign says the brake is taking energy out of the wheel

tts_sentences.text_en: The brake still presses on the wheel's rim — its turning effect, torque tau, keeps the wheel slowing.
Two counters run together: angle theta, and work W — torque times angle.
The torque meter reads minus zero point four zero newton metres: the minus sign means the brake removes energy from the wheel.

misconception_watch.belief: The wheel is slowing down, so nothing is doing work — work only happens when something speeds up.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The work counter keeps climbing the whole state, and every value it shows carries a minus sign.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The brake is doing work on the wheel; the minus sign says that work is removing energy, not adding it.

STATE_4.title: The work is the energy lost

scene_composition.text: The energy meter and the bar return beside the still-running work counter
As work grows more negative the energy bar falls by the same amount, beat for beat
like a potter's wheel slowed by a hand pressed to its rim — the brake's work is the wheel's lost energy

tts_sentences.text_en: The energy meter and the bar return, beside the work counter that never stopped running.
As the work counter grows more negative, the energy bar falls by the same amount — like a potter's wheel slowed by a hand pressed to its rim.
The brake's work is exactly the wheel's lost energy.

scene_composition.text: The rule is built line by line beside the same decaying spin
I times alpha checks against the live torque row; the closing line points at the live KE row
a torque that speeds the wheel up instead would do positive work

tts_sentences.text_en: This rule comes from adding up work as the wheel turns.
Torque equals I times alpha — check it against the live rows.
Carrying the turn through gives one half I omega squared — the rotational work-energy rule.
A torque that speeds the wheel up instead does positive work and adds energy.

scene_composition.text: Every relevant control is live — the brake torque and the seed speed
Drag the brake torque and watch theta, tau and W respond live on the same wheel
a fresh seed speed starts a fresh work count, exactly as a work ledger should

STATE_1.caption: Spinning stores energy

STATE_4.label: The energy lost is the work done
STATE_4.caption: Energy falls as work grows

STATE_6.label: Full turntable — brake torque and seed speed live
STATE_6.caption: Try it yourself
